====================Chapter 1====================
“So...”
“So it's a promise.”
“A promise between the two of us.”
“......if...”
“If the world ever comes to an end...”
“And we're the only ones left......”
*──Dark.*
*──This place is so dark.*
*The dry sound of shoes walking along the stone-paved alley. Everything else is silent.*
*No. No, that's wrong. I can hear something else. It isn't just the sound of my hasty steps.*
*It's my breathing. I'm gasping, seemingly in pain.*
*The breath of someone walking through London's darkness, through the capital of the great and prosperous British Empire. My breath.*
*There's nobody here. Is there nobody here?*
*In the midst of a silent world where only my shoes and my feet are audible, I knew that.*
*Nobody's here. I am...the only one...here.*
*The Engine Lights shine unceasingly into the darkness. The Engine Factory two streets away can be heard faintly.*
*But here, it's only me. This is the Westminster part of London. London should be a thriving city, but...*
*It's only me. I am the only living, moving thing here.*
*That can't be. That can't be.*
*I'm walking. Despite my gasps, I try in vain to breathe quietly, to walk quietly without slowing down.*
*I'm walking, because I can feel what's approaching me.*
*──Run.*
*Run.*
*Run.*
*Run.*
*The thing behind me. It's an infinite darkness, something which shouldn't be possible.*
*If the darkness catches me, it'll kill me. "That" is waiting to kill me.*
*No one can go against "that" or its fangs. Not as it both lies in wait and chases you from the darkness.*
*As long as the screams of the sacrificial girl continue, "that" can kill anyone.*
*It can kill, using the same power the girl and I both fear.*
*It kills all manner of living creatures──*
*However.*
*However...*
*If this body of mine were darkness──*
"──Now then."
*The man spoke. He was a man wearing a strange mask.*
*It looked similar to a clown's, and like a French aristocrat's from the previous century.*
*A strange person. The mask and clothes made him think that.*
*He never spoke his own name. He would only joke that he 'looked like himself'. And as his appearance suggested, he was a strange man.*
*An animal god from a small island country in Asia. That was this man's current name.*
*To be precise, the man's name was «Baron». People called him Baron Münchhausen.*
*──Of course, ──There are not many who say his name to begin with.*
*For example──*
*They say he is the leader of criminal organisations that never hesitate to kill. They say he is the head of a secret society writhing in the darkest corners of Europe.*
*You must not speak that name carelessly. If you value your life.*
*You must not imagine what lies behind that mask. If you value your life.*
*It is said that countless fictions spread from that man's mouth. That man, who now began to speak to the person before him.*
*A room with a strange pattern in its marble floor. The man sitting in the sofa and one "other" were there.*
*The room was strange, just like the man himself. A number of masks lined the old walls and bookshelves.*
*People called it a space of tranquil knowledge. The same few people who spoke the man's name.*
*A space of tranquil knowledge. In this place, it is said that even an infant's whisper would surely reach his ears.*
*A room made using knowledge from the organisation the man belonged to, which even made possible the multiple simultaneous conversations performed by a holy man of the Far East.*
*A secret room of darkness. Could it be called an altar?*
"Now then. Why don't I make an announcement?"
*──Of the beginning of the grand experiment. ──Of the beginning of profound cognisance.*
*──And the start of a new era.*
"One and only one reigns supreme in this world. Master Hermes, the leader of our «Society»."
"Also known as, Althotas Thoth Hermes."
"However, something that surpasses even the master's power..."
"Is going to descend upon the capital, upon the city protected by the Queen's impossible reign."
*There was laughter in the man's voice. The one he spoke to was silent.*
"High Agent M has already begun surveillance."
"Sooner or later, the Gates of Tartarus will open."
"If I were to express any concern, it would be that the whereabouts of the equation Master Weishaupt desires so greatly still remain unknown──"
"Did His Excellency not say that we are not to seek it out?"
*There was ridicule in the man's voice. The one he spoke to was silent.*
"I see."
"That may be the case, and it might also not be the case."
"Now..."
"All of you humans, forever loved by us. Lend me your ears."
"──Everything is about to begin."
*Echoing sounds. ^g995Echoing sounds.*
*Was it birth cries of steel that rang out from the cradle of the Engines?*
*A giant dragon of steel hidden deep underground, neither speaking nor moving.*
*The multi-connector supermassive Calculation Engine was a dragon of steel. Not many humans knew that this tunnel was called the «Engine Corridor».*
*──It should be around the same number, ──As those who knew the Baron's name.*
*For example──*
*The leaders of criminal organisations that never hesitate to kill. The head of a secret society writhing in the darkest corners of Europe.*
*Those who've attained the position of «Diogenes», at the foot of Her Highness the Queen who governs Britain.*
*Deep underneath London, countless Engines were joined together to create this tunnel. A corner of the «Engine Corridor» that forms part of the brain of Britain.*
*──Some think of it as a circuit. ──Some think of it as an altar.*
*You must never set foot in that place. If you value your life.*
*You must not even imagine what lies hidden inside. If you value your life.*
*Not one respectable human existed there. There was only darkness, black and steel.*
*A black man, and a steel woman.*
*──Within the cradle of Engines, ──The steel woman "connects".*
“......1st limiting Engine removed.”
“Confirmed increase in functionality. Retrying input to the command system.”
*──One at a time.*
*──Little by little.*
*She probably looked human to those who didn't know her. The woman looked at the body built from state-of-the-art Engines──*
*──The doll in the form of a woman looked at herself. ──At her own body.*
*Removing, equipping, connecting, one by one, little by little.*
*Regaining her functionality, while losing a part of herself.*
*The woman connected her circuits to new circuits. One by one, as if checking them individually.*
“......my master.”
*The woman's voice shook. The words were directed at the man gazing upon her.*
*The black man was silent behind her, gazing at the woman adjusting herself.*
*He dragged a number of cables towards her, slowly attaching them to the woman's back.*
“My master. I am still lacking in firepower. I cannot completely destroy the target.”
"It's fine."
*The black man spoke quietly. He touched his cold hand to the woman's cheek.*
"This is enough."
"Between you and the Kruschtya Equation, we are already──"
"I'm already..."
*The man didn't continue. He simply let silence fill the corridor.*
*After a while, the woman spoke. As if whispering. As if murmuring.*
“......yes, my master.”
*──At first, it was a whisper.*
*Someone's voice whispering in my ear, and not the voice of someone I knew.*
*I couldn't understand it. I tried to turn around, but...*
*No. I can't.*
*I felt as if I couldn't turn around. I walked a little faster instead.*
*After a while, I noticed. I wasn't in London anymore, but in a much darker, poorly lit place.*
*What should have been familiar streets were warping into bizarre shapes.*
*Horribly warped. Horribly dark.*
*What should have been a well-paved alley bent and twisted──*
*I wanted someone to save me. But then I realised there was no one there.*
*That can't be. That can't be, but...*
*I was all alone in this London of warped darkness.*
*──The whisper changes.*
*──Into a scream.*
*I broke into a run. Someone was screaming, and coming closer.*
*A scream. A scream.*
*It should be only one voice, but I heard several.*
*That terrifying scream shook my skull, numbing my thoughts. Tears suddenly fell from my eyes.*
*I tripped over something and fell to the ground. No. No. I had to run!*
*Run.*
*Run, run, run!*
*My legs wouldn't listen to me. I couldn't move a single muscle.*
*I barely had enough strength to wiggle a finger.*
*──I could hear the scream. ──Right behind my head.*
*──It's close. ──Who?*
"You......"
*I casually turned──*
*──Towards the one approaching me.*
*──I woke up with a soft sensation.*
*Synthetic silk softly touched her eyes. Someone had wiped away her tears.*
*How many times had it happened this month? Once? No, it was probably twice.*
*She hadn't fallen asleep. But she was definitely dreaming.*
*A daydream.*
*It'd been happening once every week for a whole year.*
*A soft, synthetic silk handkerchief with an Engine-made lace pattern softly touched Mary's eyes.*
*──Charlie's pure white handkerchief.*
*Charlie always did that for her. She softly wiped the tears away with her pretty handkerchief.*
Charlie: "You're crying again. Mary. Kitty. Such a crybaby."
Mary: "......sorry."
Charlie: "It's all right, don't apologise. No, don't move yet."
Mary: "......I won't."
*There was a lot Mary wanted to say to her. But even though she wanted to make excuses, she always went quiet.*
*She was supposed to be one of the most talented students in the Royal College of Scholars' history department, but... But the truth was, Mary couldn't beat Charlie.*
*──Charlie touches my cheek. ──With a soft smile on her face.*
"It's fine now. You don't need to worry," she said.
*She didn't say it out loud, but it was clearly written on the girl's face. Even though she wasn't worried or sad or anything...*
*──Charlie. ──Charlotte Brontë.*
*──One of my closest friends.*
*Prettier and smarter than all of the other girls at the College. Some also believed that her judgement was better than anyone else's.*
*The latter made her head tilt, but Mary did agree that Charlie was pretty and smart.*
*She was like an older sister, but sometimes she made childish faces like a younger sister.*
*──That's Charlie.*
*──She's been my friend for as long as I can remember.*
Charlie: "Are you feeling well?"
Mary: "Yes, I'm fine. It's nothing. Ah, but please don't call me Kitty."
Charlie: "I know, I know."
Charlie: "I will when you stop requiring my handkerchief. You adorable little Kitty."
Mary: "......please."
*A sigh. She didn't mind all that much because it was Charlie, but something did annoy her about being called Kitty.*
*But that was also normal. Just like having tea at an hour like this. Just like passing time at an hour like this.*
*Friday morning. Free time between lectures.*
*They always visited this café on Friday mornings, for elevenses and to tidy themselves.*
*They would order fragrant black tea and freshly-baked scones, and get lost in pointless conversations.*
*They would always put dollops of cream on their scones, and spend a lot of time talking.*
*They had plenty of time before afternoon lectures, as usual. So Mary composed herself, smiled and returned to the previous conversation.*
*She felt sorry for Angie, who was undoubtedly still in class, but Mary and Charlie were in a different department so nothing could be done about it.*
*On any other day, Angie would come along too. But on Fridays, it would be just the two of them.*
*──And we always, ──Have vague, rambling conversations.*
*──The kind we can't have with Angie here. ──The kind that might not be good for her upbringing.*
*──For example, ──About the latest Beardsley art.*
*──For example, ──About relationships between male and female students.*
*──For example, ──About the "lecturers" at the College.*
*──And, yes, ──A little about Angie's betrothed.*
Charlie: "Mary, did you hear? They say that Angie's beau has finally been accepted as a scholarship student."
Mary: "At Oxford?"
Charlie: "Yes. Apparently they're already deciding which field he'll be going in to. Which means he might have finally passed."
Mary: "Charlie, you're still against him courting Angie, aren't you?"
Charlie: "Nonsense. If they want to hold hands, then I'd be fine with two whole seconds."
Mary: "......I think that means you're against it."
Charlie: "But I'm not against it."
*──Angie. Cute Angelica. ──She's like our little sister.*
*──When it comes to Angie, ──Charlie starts acting like an overprotective mother.*
Charlie: "But what about you? Has anything happened yet? I'm still waiting."
Mary: "You mean with a man?"
Charlie: "Yes."
Mary: "......don't be silly. I have no plans for that at the moment. Besides, Charlie, you haven't exactly..."
Charlie: "Oh? Really? Do you think I'm going to be alone forever?"
Mary: "Eh?"
Charlie: "I'm teasing you. You and Angie are far more fun to drink tea with."
Mary: "......don't scare me like that."
*That surprised her. Charlie could tell jokes like that with a perfectly straight face, so Mary had to be careful.*
*Looking at her soft smile, yes, Mary thought it really was a joke.*
*Even when she was joking, Charlie still gave in when she looked into her eyes.*
*So it was fine. What she said just now really was a joke.*
Charlie: "But what about Mr Heger? He seems interested in you."
Mary: "You mean Heinz?"
Charlie: "Yes. That "noble German youth". And I hear he's close to the first professor."
Mary: "I...see. He does have a nice face. But no, I can't, not him."
Mary: "......indeed, I might feel the same way."
Charlie: "Same as...?"
Mary: "You, Charlie. I'm not interested in courting right now either."
Charlie: "Oh? Such a waste......"
Mary: "Same goes for you, you know. You're so preoccupied with other people."
Charlie: "I can't help that. Both your mother and Angie's are trusting me to take care of you."
Mary: "......and our potential partners?"
Charlie: "Yes?"
Mary: "Fine."
*She shrugged her shoulders. Out of the three of them, Charlie was the best at suddenly changing the topic.*
*Part of that had to be luck. For example, right now──*
Claudia: "I heard you. What were you saying about the German exchange student?"
Claudia: "That man is so handsome. He's like a rose."
Mary: "......not you too."
*And the previous topic had returned. Claudia was the café's owner, and she troubled Mary in the same way Charlie did.*
*When Mary left for London, her mother asked four people to keep an eye on her. One of them was Charlie──*
*──The owner of this café was another. ──Lady Claudia.*
Claudia: "I love his dulled hair and melancholic eyes. So, Mary, is he courting you?"
Mary: "......no. There's nothing going on, really. Stop teasing me, both of you."
Claudia: "I thought you'd be happy. Right?"
Charlie: "Lady Claudia's right. Isn't she, Mary?"
Mary: "......fine."
*A sigh. She shrugged her shoulders and brought the teacup to her lips.*
*Every woman close to her mother was good at troubling Mary, no matter what her age. Everyone but her uncle.*
Claudia: "Back when she was your age, your mother was quite popular you know. Not as much as myself, of course."
Charlie: "Ah, could you tell us more about that? For future reference."
Mary: "W-wait a moment, Charlie."
Claudia: "Well, this one time──"
Bell: "Lady Claudiaaa! We're out of Darjeeling tea! P-please help!"

Charlie: "Yes, some other time. I look forward to it, Lady."

Charlie: "Hm?"

Charlie: "Speaking of stories, Mary. How much more have you written?"

*No such things existed. They were nothing more than rumours.*

*And──*

*──I softly push on my right eyelid. ──As if hiding it.*

*A golden eye. The doctor said there was no sign of illness, but she was having these bad dreams.*

*──1905. ──People call it the radiant and glorious 20th century.*

*──I like it too.*

*They belched out smoke which filled the sky. He glared angrily at them──*
Holmes: "──Well then."
Holmes: "I take it you're satisfied with this now. Not to mention what Diogenes thinks."
*Those weren't words for the old man. He was muttering to himself.*
*Holmes' gaze didn't move in the slightest as he continued.*
Holmes: "There needs to be someone to destroy illusions. In order for us humans to continue to be human."
Holmes: "In order for endless prosperity to continue. In order for us to have endless dreams. In order for us to make those things happen with our own hands."
Professor: "Even if the tomorrow that awaits you is one where gunfire, screams, despair, and fearsome weapons fill the skies, Sherlock Holmes?"
Holmes: "Yes, Professor James Moriarty."
*Holmes answered his silent question. He looked away from the window──*
*He slid his hand inside his coat. He grabbed something.*
Holmes: "It's time we end this. Her Majesty will have to hide herself before long. You're the only player left in London now."
Professor: "......I see."
Professor: "Don't we need to do this at a waterfall? Are you going to deny the necessary «facts of history» yourself?"
Holmes: "I'll tell Watson about it when he returns. The Reichenbach Falls are too far from here."
*And then──*
*──One gunshot.*
*After that──*
*Time flowed──*
*Several seasons passed.*
*A few months? Half a year? A whole year? Even longer? ^g995Or perhaps much, much longer than that.*
*It was around the time when Queen Victoria suddenly announced she was abdicating the throne through a public relations official.*
*London was in an uproar. However, there weren't as many changes as the people imagined.*
*Time flowed steadily onwards, and the people adapted to the era called the 20th century.*
*Steadily, at times rapidly. Engine Machines changed, but the people did not.*
*Not today. Not tomorrow. They continued their small, ephemeral lives.*
*Statistically speaking, crime showed no sign of decreasing, and the dark rumours of the high rise buildings didn't die out. Despite that, they believed in a tomorrow better than today.*
*Rumours──*
*Yes, rumours too.*
*From today to tomorrow, rumours shifted and changed.*
*The people no longer said much of the «Metacreature» rumours.*
*The military power balance crumbled during the Engine Weapon development race── Such unsettling rumours began to be whispered.*
*Day and night, the tabloids listed rumours about Engine Weapon development in all the countries of the globe.*
*However──*
*That was not all. It wasn't just things which gave dark implications.*
*There'd been a confirmed increase in the number of "gaps" in the sky. The light brought about by the sky behind the drifting grey clouds was a temporary relief to people accustomed to smoke.*
*A pair of Scholars at the University of Paris succeeded at developing Engines using a new kind of energy. There were newspaper articles saying sensational things about it.*
*The 20th century had only just begun. No one knew what would happen tomorrow.*
*Who would end up marrying who? Whose child would speak words first? No one knew such trivial things.*
*No one knew what would happen on trivial, but happy tomorrows.*
*No one──*
*──It was the same for me. ──I never thought I'd get this lucky.*
*──A destined meeting? ──Yes, that's right, I think that's it.*
*──It happened right after the Queen abdicated. ──I suddenly had a stroke of luck.*
*For some reason, a publishing company figured that a merchant would have good stories to tell, and Mr Howard received a request to write a novel──*
*He said he knew someone perfect for the job, and introduced Mary to that company.*
*Howard himself had no interest in making a book, and was too busy with his job and Angie anyway. Or so he said.*
*──But it's just too sudden. ──I was writing something completely different.*
*──A picture book. ──At least until now I was...*
*There was some confusion after the editor who saw her picture book said they'd take care of the text and pictures if she put out a horror novel.*
*But at long last, the small company published a single picture book.*
*──A very small run. ──Only one thousand copies.*
*──Printed on the latest Printing Engine. ──One thousand small records of me.*
*──They didn't actually sell that well. ──A lot were left over.*
*──But I don't mind. ──Yes, it's all right.*
*──Because I wanted to tell as many people as possible besides my friends.*
*──What I saw. ──Everything I've seen with these eyes up until now.*
*──Beautiful things. ──Wonderful things. ──And terrifying things as well.*
*──All of it. ──I wanted someone other than me to see it.*
Mary: "......one, two, three. I'm getting a lot more of these than I expected."
*Two months after the picture book was published──*
*First a couple of envelopes reached her. What one would call fan letters.*
*Apparently the publisher had sent them to her directly, but there were others piled up they were planning to send later. That was what her editor told her.*
*Her editor also told her this. Just the other day, one or two suspicious envelopes came in, so the company was discussing what to do with them.*
*──They were scared, so they must have wanted to get rid of them quickly.*
*──Did they really discuss it with everyone? ──I'm a little worried, but...*
*──But I'm glad they sent them to me. ──It'd be bad if these got thrown out.*
*Anyway... Anyway... A few fan letters that had safely reached her.*
*She organised the books and lecture notes filling her desk, then decided to clean her entire room while she was at it as a nice change of pace.*
*All of today's envelopes had reached her in the morning, but by the time she got around to reading them, it was almost noon.*
Mary: "......all right, time to read them."
*She opened the envelopes one by one with her usual letter opener.*
*The first one──*
*──The first letter was from Angie. ──A well-thought out opinion of my book, and an energetic summary of how she was doing.*
*──Complaints about and love for Mr Howard. ──And many words for me.*
Mary: "You wrote so much...... But you said you had lots of homework left to do."
Mary: "......thank you, Angie."
*The second one──*
*──The second one was from Elly. ──I never saw her handwriting before.*
*──Awkward, but also warm. ──It felt like her, the way she said what she thought of the book.*
*──The subject suddenly changed halfway through. ──From her journey to Celenaria in Southern Kadath, ──To a diary about life in an airship guild.*
Mary: "An airship guild? That girl...she really is...flying......"
Mary: "Amazing. You've come so close to your dream."
Mary: "Look at me from up there in the sky someday, Elly."
*The third one──*
*──The third one was from Charlie. ──Familiar handwriting. Slender and pretty.*
*──Her opinions of the book were simply embarrassing. ──She also encouraged me to write more.*
*──And she told me what had happened in Central Northern Kadath, where she'd gone to finish recuperating. ──Few words, but a definite message.*
Mary: "......Charlie."
Mary: "Angie and I will come see you someday. Just wait for us."
*Yes, in spring──*
*She would have time in the spring, so she decided to go there with a huge travel suitcase. She also decided to visit her mother's workplace.*
*She left a note to herself to write a reply. She started planning the trip in her head.*
*After a short while, she reached for the next envelope.*
*There was also a letter from Viola. Elegant, conscientious, kind words, just like the woman herself.*
*Ones from Bell, and Donna, and Claudia too. And from Mrs Hudson, and Uncle George, and others.*
*Even from her mother──*
*And then...*
*And then...*
*Letters from children she'd never seen before.*
*Several opinions from children who'd read the book. Some poorly written letters, and some pretty ones probably written by their parents──*
*──I read all of them carefully. ──Leaving notes to myself to respond to each one.*
*She opened the bottom drawer of her desk and slid them into a beautifully decorated folder.*
*A drawer where she put what was precious to her. There were lots of memories in there as well.*
*──The book Moran gave me. ──The book Jane gave me too. They're here now.*
*──Every time I see them, I remember. ──Even if everyone else forgets them...*
*──I won't. ──At the very least, I won't forget.*
Mary: "......now then."
*She prepared herself a little,*
*and picked up the last remaining envelope.*
*What could it possibly be? Insults, maybe? She doubted it had any explosives or poisons in it.*
*The last envelope her publishing company considered destroying. That envelope had no sender name.*
*Even on the inside──*
*There was only a single piece of white paper. Instead of an address──*
*There was one line──*
"October 5th, at the water's edge."
Mary: "October......"
*──Suddenly, I remember. ──That day in October, 1905.*
*──The day we first met. ──But...*
*──But this isn't the exact day I remember. ──I'm sure I met him on the 6th or 7th.*
*──Someone else?*
*──When I heard about a suspicious envelope, I thought of him right away. ──But, it's not him?*
*Mary held the white paper in silence for a while──*
*Her right eye told her on its own. She wasn't mistaken.*
*She hadn't felt this sensation in a while. Her golden eye told her something all on its own.*
*She wasn't mistaken. She wasn't mistaken. Mary didn't know his handwriting, but...*
*He'd written this. She was sure he'd looked up at the sky as he wrote.*
*She didn't know if he was alive. Or even if he was human.*
*──Is that you? ──You, who those two women said was human.*
*──You who wished and yearned for something. ──You who searched for something.*
*──You who touched this letter in my hands. ──You who were loved by two different people.*
*──You who said you'd read Dumas. ──James.*
Mary: "Yes, that's right."
Mary: "This is a quote from Dumas......"
*October 5th──*
*It wasn't that day, that night, that day they'd met. It wasn't even a real date.*
*It wasn't obvious, but it was definitely a message from him.*
Mary: "......you're near water, aren't you?"
*October 5th──*
*That date came from Dumas' magnum opus. The final chapter──*
Charlie: "......you're amazing, Mary."
Charlie: "You're not afraid of anything. Anything at all......"
Charlie: "So...... How about the Shadow Builder, from that fairy tale?"
Mary: "Who's he?"
Charlie: "The pastor at church told me about him. He was a black shadow......"
Charlie: "And he disappeared when God said "let there be light"......"
Charlie: "So the Shadow Builder has a grudge against humans who live in bright places."
Charlie: "He does scary things...... He's the reason the night is so scary."
Mary: "I'm not scared of him."
Charlie: "......really......?"
Mary: "Really. After all, he listened to God's words, didn't he?"
Mary: "So he understands language. If he does, then yes, I'm not scared."
Mary: "It'll be fine if I can just talk to him! I'm good at making friends."
Mary: "Aren't I?"
*──The little girl smiled──*
*──Holding her friend's hand──*
Mary: "I even became friends with you, Charlie. I know I'm good at this."
Mary: "I can become friends with anyone."
*──The smiling girl──*
*──Said that──*
*──And within her shadow──*
*──A red eye warped──*
*──As if looking at something bright──*
